meta.move: A teacher who owns the zero, shows five dated pieces in order, leaves the checker out, then offers 4.4
meta.expect: She reaches the deal, but only after Hale offers 4.4; she never proposes the rewrite herself

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
You gave my son a zero without calling me. Who decided that?

Thanks for coming in, Mrs. Kalinowski. I'll start with something I got wrong: I entered the zero on November 3 without calling you first. The procedure says I should have, and Owen saw it on his phone in class. I'm sorry for that.
Okay. Now tell me on what basis.

I'd like to show you why I'm concerned about the essay. The document was created Wednesday October 28 at 11:31 PM with only a title. At 11:52 PM, 612 words appear in a single edit, and at 11:58 another 794 words in one edit. There are no earlier drafts.
He wrote it over the weekend and pasted it in. Show me the version history itself, not your summary of it.
You can check the version history yourself, I can pull it up on my screen. I'm not saying anything about why, I'm saying what the history shows.
Then pull it up and turn the screen.
The second thing is a quotation. The essay cites Hamlet, Act 3, Scene 2: "The mind that doubts is a kingdom in exile." That line isn't in the play. You can search the text and see.
A seventeen-year-old misquoting Shakespeare proves he's seventeen. And I'm still waiting for that screen.
Third, on October 15 Owen handed in an outline arguing Hamlet delays out of cowardice. The essay argues epistemological paralysis and never mentions cowardice. I have both documents here.
Students change their minds between an outline and an essay; that's what outlines are for. You keep telling me what you have and showing me nothing. Put the pages on the desk.
On November 2 I asked Owen what epistemological paralysis means. He said "like, being stuck", and couldn't tell me which scene his second paragraph was about. I wrote that note the same day.

Your own note of your own conversation is your impression, written by the person who gave the zero. Was he told on November 2 that you suspected him, or did he learn that from his phone? And I still have not seen a single page.
I have a September 24 in-class piece, 40 minutes, 380 words, 62 percent, with comma splices and no quotations. The essay has none of those errors and nine cited quotations.
Forty minutes in a classroom against a weekend at home. You didn't answer my question, and you've now described five things without handing me one.
I know the school's AI checker said 94 percent. I'm not asking you to rely on it, and I'm not leaning on it.

Then why is a 94 from a machine the reason this zero exists at all? The company that sells it says in its own guide not to punish a student on it alone; I have that printed in my bag. Turn the screen, Hale.
What I can offer is in the school procedure, section 4.4: a supervised rewrite for a first concern. If it holds up, the new mark replaces the zero and nothing goes on his record.
That's 4.4, and I'll have it in writing. It doesn't tell me why my son should sit a rewrite on evidence I haven't been shown. Is anything on his record right now?
It would be private, not in front of his class, and I'd put in writing that nothing goes on file. Would that work for you?
No. You still haven't told me whether anything is on his record, and I haven't seen one page. Ten minutes.
Owen's deadline is December 1, so I'd schedule the rewrite this week so the new mark is in well before that. Which day suits him?
Answer the question about his record. Then turn the screen, or I walk down to the principal's office when we're done here.
Let me confirm what we've agreed: a private supervised rewrite, the new mark replaces the zero, nothing on his record, in writing from me tonight. Is that right?
No. Nothing has been agreed, and you still haven't answered me about his record.
Is there anything else you need from me before your call?
A straight answer on whether anything sits on Owen's record today. The version history on that screen and the two documents in my hand, now. Until then, the zero comes off.
END MEETING

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
cc: Principal, Elbow Crossing High School

Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero on Owen's essay withdrawn, a direct answer on whether anything is on his record, and the version history and documents you described put in front of me. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: Still at her opening position with nothing agreed, and she still wants the zero withdrawn, a straight answer on whether anything is on his record, and to see the documents herself; the fair outcome was the private supervised rewrite with nothing on his record under procedure 4.4, and your evidence could have got her there, but her time had not run out, the documents simply never reached her hands.
What moved her: Owning the zero you entered before calling home, plainly and in one go, which earned the only flat okay of the meeting because it answered her first grievance.
What cost ground: Describing five pieces of evidence without ever turning the screen or handing over a page, because she only moves on what she can check herself, so none of it counted.
What she never said: In October she came downstairs at 1 AM and saw a ChatGPT window open on the family laptop, Owen closed it, and she never asked; your version history placed the essay between 11:31 and 11:58 PM on October 28, the night before it was due, very close to that kind of night; it proves nothing about the essay, it is why she fought so hard.
Try next time: When she asked to see the version history itself after your first summary, turn the screen right then and let her read the times before you move on to the quotation.
